Definition: Water that flows downhill along a path, from where it starts to where it ends.
The line a river follows, made of points you place on the ground.
One place on a river's path. The river runs from its first point to its last.
The ground under a river's water, cut lower than the ground around it.
The ground at the side of a river, which holds the water in.
Lowering the ground under a river to make its bed and banks.
The direction a river's water flows: from its first point toward its last.
Keeping only the details that matter for a problem. A river's few points stand in for every drop of its water.
